approved: Health Insurance Legislation Amendment (Assignment of Medicare Benefits) Bill 2024
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would update rules for assigning Medicare benefits in bulk-billed and simplified billing services to reduce upfront costs for patients and administrative burdens for providers.
It would allow patients to assign their Medicare benefit before or after a service, enable ongoing assignments, and let regulations replace approved forms with prescribed information.
The bill would remove imprisonment for failing to provide a copy of an assignment and reduce civil penalties from 10 to 5 penalty units.
Allow assignment of Medicare benefit before or after a service is rendered.
Enable enduring (ongoing) assignment agreements for future services.
Shift the duty to retain a copy of the assignment agreement from the patient to the practitioner.
Require practitioners, insurers or billing agents to notify patients about claims on assigned benefits.
Remove the requirement for practitioners to co-sign an assignment agreement.
Reduce civil penalties from 10 to 5 penalty units and remove imprisonment for failing to provide a copy of an assignment.
Patients, health service providers, practitioners, private health insurers, approved billing agents, hospitals, and the Chief Executive of Medicare.
Health Insurance Legislation Amendment (Assignment of Medicare Benefits) Act 2024
